fractal D is a useful measure of arrhythmia recurrence risk in patients with ventricular arrhythmia.

the fractal D of VPC occurrence predicts arrhythmia recurrences in patients with life-threatening ventricular tachyarrhythmias, that it is a powerful predictor of arrhythmia recurrence in patients with a wide variety of arrhythmia types, and that it is a more accurate predictor than the frequency of arrhythmia occurrence.

fractal D is an independent predictor of VT recurrence in patients with life-threatening ventricular tachyarrhythmias, and that this prediction is superior to the prediction obtained with other Holter variables.

the development of new techniques for the analysis of Holter recordings.
the study of the dynamics of cardiac arrhythmias, with particular emphasis on the analysis of the temporal patterns of ventricular premature complexes.
the development of new methods for the diagnosis and management of cardiac arrhythmias, with the ultimate objective of improving the outcome of patients suffering from these conditions.

the presence of complex VPC patterns, including couplets and runs of VT, in a patient being treated for sustained ventricular arrhythmia is associated with a high probability of arrhythmia recurrence and death.
the presence of a high number of VPCs, a high number of runs of VT, and a high number of couplets are all independent and additive predictors of arrhythmic events in the postinfarction period.
the use of fractal D in patients with ventricular arrhythmia is a very useful tool for predicting arrhythmic events.
